system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped in aggregate at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m). | A materially higher general cap, ideally 100% of price, or at least a cap calibrated to the diligence risks and available recovery. | **Reject 20%; seek a substantially higher cap** because the disclosed exposures could make a AUD 4.8m ceiling inadequate. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim and AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with recovery only above the basket. | A lower de minimis and basket, preferably a tipping basket so the full amount is recoverable once crossed; exclude specified, fundamental, tax and indemnity claims as appropriate. | **Seek a lower de minimis and tipping basket** because the proposed deductible-style basket leaves the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying loss. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notify general Warranty Claims within 18 months after Completion; Seller proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise. | A longer general warranty survival period (for example, 24–36 months), with separate longer periods for tax and other claims, and no blanket extension of the general limit to all Claims. | **Seek 24–36 months and express category-specific periods** because different claim types need different survival periods and discovery timelines. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate, substantially higher cap (ideally price), longer survival, and appropriate carve-outs from thresholds and other general limitations. | **Reject the general regime for fundamental/title claims** because ownership and authority are core to receiving the bargain. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions stated to apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is identified. | Expressly exclude fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation (including applicable seller-side attribution) from caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance protections, to the extent legally permissible. | **Require an express fraud carve-out** because the draft’s broad limitations could otherwise be argued to restrict remedies for deliberate wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Limit disclosure to fair, specific disclosure in the Disclosure Letter that identifies the nature and reasonably ascertainable scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure and require particularised disclosure** because blanket incorporation can qualify warranties for matters the Buyer may not have identified or understood. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No general buyer-knowledge bar; at most, narrowly define actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable inquiry, excluding constructive or imputed knowledge. | **Delete the broad qualifier** because “discoverable” knowledge creates uncertainty and rewards inadequate disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty written consent. Disclosure says final consent and evidence of associated condition satisfaction are absent. | Make valid consent and satisfaction/waiver of all clause 11.3 conditions a condition precedent to Completion, with no deemed satisfaction merely on delivery of a consent letter. | **Require verified consent and condition compliance before Completion** because Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and the disclosure confirms the evidence is missing. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m facility to be addressed by a release provided after Completion; it remains outstanding and no final security discharge is in the data room. | Repayment and release/discharge of the facility and security at or before Completion, with any payoff funded and reflected in debt-free/cash-free price mechanics. | **Make repayment and effective release a Completion requirement** because a post-Completion promise leaves the Buyer exposed to debt and continuing security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are treated as Seller’s matter and omitted from the funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unspecified. | Identify and account for the bonuses and all associated on-costs as debt-like/leakage or an agreed price adjustment, with payment mechanics and responsibility expressly allocated. | **Resolve and include the full cost in the funds flow or adjustment** because the disclosed conditional liabilities are omitted and may be larger than AUD 420,000. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-004 requires cleared payment of every SOW3 fee for transfer, while DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Expand protection to cover all amounts, title/ownership, transfer, use and enforcement of required Project Materials, with payment/assignment evidence or escrow/holdback before Completion. | **Do not accept the narrow indemnity as adequate** because the disclosed open balance and missing assignment leave material uncertainty over ownership and usable IP. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; Seller proposes ordinary limitations. Disclosure records an unintended external email and potentially 1,240 records, with access, scope and notification still unknown. | Obtain completed investigation and remediation/notification assessment before Completion, specific warranties and an uncapped or separately capped indemnity for incident-related liabilities, costs and claims. | **Treat this as a specific risk, not a presumed immateriality** because the scope and access remain unresolved and could create regulatory, remediation and customer exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 described as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure says their timing and scope must be read together but does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Verify terms, commitments, termination rights, accruals and approval; include unavoidable pre-Completion commitments in debt-like items or specific protections. | **Require contract-level review and clear price treatment** because the disclosure does not establish that the full AUD 330,000 is ordinary-course or avoidable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance provisions apply to Claims of any nature; Seller says tax and IP are settled under the general regime. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and fraud, with tailored caps, thresholds and periods. | **Reject an all-Claims limitation regime** because distinct risks require distinct remedies and survival periods. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register as evidence that it holds 100% of issued shares. | Verify title independently through current company records and execution/transfer mechanics; obtain warranties of full legal and beneficial ownership, no encumbrances and authority to transfer. | **Do not treat the register alone as complete verification** because the disclosure identifies its source but expressly does not say Buyer has verified title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime. | Negotiate express tax and IP warranties and tailored claim regimes; tax should have an appropriate cap and survival period tied to the relevant assessment period, while IP protection should address ownership, infringement and required rights. | **Keep both categories open pending express terms** because the Seller’s assertion does not supply the protections or tailored limits the Buyer needs. |
=== END ADVICE ===
